input: Start a sourdough starter from scratch at home

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the goal is just to establish an active starter or to also bake a first loaf changes how far the plan needs to extend.
A complete beginner needs step-by-step rationale and troubleshooting, while someone who has baked bread before needs less foundational explanation.
A starter typically takes 7-14 days; knowing if the user has a deadline (e.g., wants to bake in a week) affects the feeding schedule and flour choices recommended.
The type of flour available (whole wheat, rye, all-purpose) significantly affects how quickly the starter activates and what method to recommend.
Kitchen temperature is the single biggest variable in fermentation speed; a warm vs. cold home requires very different feeding frequencies and timing.
Whether the user has a kitchen scale affects whether instructions should use weight (grams) or volume (cups/tablespoons), which impacts consistency.
Some users want a small, low-maintenance starter; others want a large, highly active one for frequent baking — this changes the target hydration, quantity, and maintenance routine.

gold.taskTitle: Build a sourdough starter from scratch at home
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to create and maintain a sourdough starter from scratch at home, capturing wild yeast to eventually bake with.

questions.title: Is your goal just an active starter, or to bake a first loaf too?
questions.description: Determines whether the plan ends at an established starter or extends into a first bake.

questions.title: How familiar are you with bread baking or fermentation?
questions.description: Calibrates the level of explanation and troubleshooting guidance needed in the plan.

questions.title: Do you have a target date you want the starter ready by?
questions.description: Affects the recommended method, flour type, and feeding schedule to hit the deadline.

questions.title: What types of flour do you currently have at home?
questions.description: Flour type (rye, whole wheat, all-purpose) directly determines activation speed and the best starting method.

questions.title: How warm does your kitchen typically stay, in general terms?
questions.description: Kitchen temperature is the biggest driver of fermentation speed and dictates feeding frequency.

questions.title: Do you have a kitchen scale to measure ingredients by weight?
questions.description: Determines whether instructions should use grams or volume cups/tablespoons for consistency.

questions.title: How much starter do you want to maintain on an ongoing basis?
questions.description: Sets the target quantity and hydration level, shaping the long-term maintenance routine.
